petition_no: APPEAL NO. 265 OF 2013 & IA NO. 357 OF 2013 & IA NO. 110 OF 2014 & IA NO. 159 OF 2015 and APPEAL NO. 266 OF 2013 & IA NO. 358 OF 2013 & IA NO. 160 OF2015
summary: In the affidavit, filed on behalf of the Appellants dated 24.02.2025, it is stated that a total of 53 issues/ heads of claims were raised by the Appellants at the time of filing of the Appeals; subsequently, there were two developments (a) the judgment passed by this Tribunal in Appeal No. 301 of 2015 dated 28.01.2025, and (b) the true-up order passed by the DERC in Petition No. 3 of 2022 dated 19.07.2024 for true-up of expenses of the Appellant for FY 2020-21. Para 4, of the said affidavit dated 24.02.2025, records the submission of the Appellants that, in the light of the judgment of this Tribunal in Appeal No. 301 of 2015 and the true-up order dated 19.07.2024, the current status of the claims were as under:- (a) Category A.1 and D comprised 9 (nine) issues which had either been implemented by the DERC or had become infructuous, and no further adjudication was required; (b) Categories A.2, B and C comprised of 14 (fourteen) claims that were covered by the judgement of this Tribunal and/ or that of the Supreme Court, as regards which(i) 1 (one) claim, i.e. Issue No. 35 in Category C had already been allowed by the DERC in Tariff Order dated 29.09.2015 for 2015-16, and no further adjudication was required; (ii) 3 (three) claims i.e. Issue Nos. 10, 11 and 41 in Category B had been partially implemented by the DERC in the true-up order dated 19.07.2024; the said claims were also pending before the Supreme Court in Contempt Petitions and/ or Miscellaneous Application(s); issue of partial implementation had been raised in Appeal (DFR) No. 530 of 2024 filed by the Appellant against the True-Up order dated 19.07.2024; the Appellant was not pressing for their adjudication in the present appeal, and liberty may be granted to raise these issues in appropriate proceedings;(iii) 3 (three) claims i.e. Issue Nos. 5, 20 and 26 in Category C had been implemented by the DERC in the True-up order dated 19.07.2024; the Appellant was not pressing for their adjudication in the present appeal, and liberty may be granted to raise those issues in appropriate proceedings, if any, inter alia regarding the manner of implementation by the DERC; and (iv) for the remaining 7 (seven) claims, being issue Nos. 4, 13, 28 and 46 in Category A.2 and Issue Nos. 30, 31 and 43 in Category B which remained unimplemented, this Tribunal may direct the DERC to implement the directions of this Tribunal and/ or Supreme Court, and to grant necessary impact along with carrying cost to the Appellant as was sought by the Appellant by way of oral submissions, claim-wise submissions tendered on 06.07.2023 as well as in the written submissions dated 03.05.2024; and these had not been disputed by the DERC at any stage of the proceedings. this Tribunal; and the claims may be disposed of with directions to abide by the Supreme Court’s directions that would be passed on the said issues. In Para 4(g), of the affidavit dated 24.02.2025, the Appellant stated that Category-I comprised of 20 (twenty) claims which were argued in detail before this Tribunal; and the status of the said claims was as under: - (i) 1 (one) claim i.e. Issue No. 17 had been implemented by the DERC in True-up order dated 19.07.2024; however, there were certain grievances for which the Appellant had filed Review Petition before the DERC which was pending adjudication; the Appellant was not pressing for their adjudication in the present appeal; and liberty may be granted to raise this issue in appropriate proceedings; (ii) 3 (three) claims i.e. Issue Nos. 24(b), 24(f) and 33 were covered by the judgment of this Tribunal in Appeal No. 301 of 2015 dated 28.01.2025 wherein a similar relief was to be allowed to the Appellants which were as under: - (a) Issue No. 24(b): Unscheduled Interchange Interest (arises only in Appeal No. 265 of 2013) – similar Issue No. 29 (Erroneous inclusion of interest on account of late payment of UI charges) was decided in favour of TPDDL while relying on the Matching Principle; (b) Issue No. 24(f) – Consideration of Income earned on Maintenance of Assets of MCD – similar Issue No. 43 (Wrong Reversal of Material Cost of Rs.3.36 Crores and Rs.4.12 Crores incurred towards maintenance of streetlight for the Year 2010-11 and 2011-12 respectively) decided in favour of TPDDL; and (c) Issue No. 33 – Disallowance of Trading Margin – similar Issue No. 22 (Wrongful disallowance of trading margin paid to TPTCL) was decided in favour of TPDDL. In Para 6(c), the Appellant seeks directions to the DERC to (i) allow the claims in para 4(g)(ii) with respect to Issue Nos. 24(b), 24(f) and 33 (in Category-I), following the judgment in Appeal No. 301 of 2015 and grant necessary impact to the Appellant along with carrying cost; and (ii) implement the judgments of this Tribunal and the Supreme Court in letter and spirit, as regards the claims detailed in Para 4(b)(iv) above i.e. Issue Nos. 4, 13, 28, 46 in Category A.2 and Issue Nos. 30, 31 and 43 in Category B; and to allow entitlements to the Appellant along with carrying cost in the next tariff proceedings. In so far as Issue Nos. 4, 13, 28 and 46 in Category A.2 and Issue Nos. 30, 31, 43 in Category B are concerned, the Appellants’ grievance is that these seven claims have not been implemented by the DERC despite the directions of this Tribunal and the Supreme Court. While making it clear that orders of this Tribunal which have attained finality, and the orders of the Supreme Court, necessitate strict adherence and must be implemented by the Commission, we leave it open to the Appellant if they are so aggrieved by its non-implementation, to agitate their grievances in appropriate proceedings. The submission, urged on behalf of the DERC, is that the Appellants had in the petition filed by them before the Commission, thereafter in the Appeal, and later in their submissions during the course of arguments before this Tribunal, made submissions that were inconsistent with each other.
title: BSES YAMUNA POWER LIMITED VERSUS DELHI ELECTRICITY REGULATORY COMMISSION & Anr
